statement: There are a smooth complex surface Y , a proper holomorphic map p : Y → ∆R, and a holomorphic section disjoint from its critical point, with the following properties. The central fiber is a reduced irreducible rational curve with one ordinary node, and every other fiber is a smooth elliptic curve. On the regular part there are coordinates, relative to the section, (8.2) z = a + τ(s)b (mod Z + τ(s)Z), (a, b) ∈ R2 /Z2 , and ds ∧ dz extends as a nowhere-zero holomorphic two-form. The real group H2(Y ; R) is generated by a regular fiber. Fix h ∈ C \ {0}, put Σ = h ds ∧ dz, and fix 0 < r < R. For every sufficiently small ϵ > 0 there is a Kähler form Dloc ϵ on Y , with metric gϵ, such that (8.3) Dloc ϵ ∧ Re Σ = Dloc ϵ ∧ Im Σ = 0, (Dloc ϵ )2 = (Re Σ)2 , ∫︂ p−1(s) Dloc ϵ = ϵ (s ̸= 0). These three forms are parallel, mutually orthogonal and of equal square, and volgϵ = (Re Σ)2/2. Moreover: (i) On each fixed closed annulus K = {r− ≤ |s| ≤ r+} ⊂ ∆R \ {0}, the form (8.4) Dsf ϵ = ϵ da ∧ db + |h|2 ϵ τ2(s) dx1 ∧ dx2, s = x1 + ix2, is well-defined and closed. For every integer m ≥ 0, in fixed smooth charts on this annular bundle, (8.5) ∥Dloc ϵ − Dsf ϵ ∥Cm ≤ Cme−cm/ϵ , Cm, cm > 0. (ii) These forms have the same real cohomology class on p−1(K). Their periods are ϵ on a fiber and zero on the torus sweeping the invariant a-circle at b = 0 around the base annulus. That swept torus bounds in Y . (iii) On p−1(∆r), for every fixed m there is a finite coordinate cover with smaller concentric domains still covering this set, such that the number of charts, the reciprocals of their radii and interior margins, and the Cm bounds for the metric coefficients and their inverses are at most Cmϵ−Nm . All intrinsic curvature derivatives of fixed finite order have polynomial bounds as well. All disks, annuli and h are fixed before ϵ tends to zero. The charts in (iii) may depend on ϵ.
